# drvPath cases for drvpath-cases.sh: a label, then an expression for a
# derivation.  `pkgs` is the pinned nixpkgs for x86_64-linux with no user
# config or overlays, and a relative path resolves against this directory.
#
# A drvPath covers its whole build-time closure, so a case earns its place
# by reaching nixpkgs code the others do not, and nova-nix's evaluation is
# the cost to weigh it against.

# The original oracle pair: the stdenv bootstrap under hello, and
# input-derivation-modulo substitution through a multi-output input.
hello            pkgs.hello
dependent        import ./dependent.nix

# What evaluation itself writes or fetches.
tofile           import ./tofile.nix
fetchgit         import ./fetchgit.nix

# Other stdenv layers: no C compiler, the i686 and musl bootstraps, and
# the LLVM toolchain.
stdenvNoCC       pkgs.stdenvNoCC
i686-hello       pkgs.pkgsi686Linux.hello
musl-hello       pkgs.pkgsMusl.hello
clang            pkgs.clang

# Cross-compiled, to another Linux and to Windows.
aarch64-hello    pkgs.pkgsCross.aarch64-multiplatform.hello
mingwW64-hello   pkgs.pkgsCross.mingwW64.hello

# Inputs selected by output name, across many multi-output packages.
curl             pkgs.curl
systemd          pkgs.systemd

# Fixed-output fetchers past fetchurl: fetchgit, fetchFromGitHub with a
# vendored cargo tree, a vendored Go module tree, fetchPypi.
sbsigntool       pkgs.sbsigntool
ripgrep          pkgs.ripgrep
fzf              pkgs.fzf
python-requests  pkgs.python3Packages.requests

# Structured attributes: one __json object in place of a variable per
# attribute, with the four outputs it names.
libxo            pkgs.libxo

# A NixOS module evaluation, down to the initrd it assembles.
nixos-initrd     (import <nixpkgs/nixos> { system = "x86_64-linux"; configuration = { fileSystems."/".device = "/dev/sda1"; boot.loader.grub.device = "/dev/sda"; system.stateVersion = "24.11"; }; }).config.system.build.initialRamdisk
